readerTitle: You have $10,000 to launch. Where does it go?
caseNote: 가상 시뮬레이션: 골판지 상자 제조 공장이 소규모 온라인 판매자용 상자 주문 웹사이트를 출시하는 이야기 (제조 + 디지털). 모든 수치는 설명용
insight: 출시 예산은 '어디에 쓸까' 하나의 질문이 아니라 누구에게, 어떤 조합으로, 얼마나 자주, 어디가 새는지를 순서대로 정하는 결정이다. 앞의 결정이 뒤의 선택지를 좁힌다.
misconception: 마케팅 예산은 많은 사람에게 한 번에 보여줄수록 효과가 크고, 결과가 나쁘면 광고를 더 사면 된다.

sources.text: 마케팅 기본 개념 (세분화·타깃·포지셔닝, 페이드·온드·언드 미디어, 도달과 빈도, 퍼널)

factChecks.note: 예산 계산: 샘플 $3,000(판매자 60명 × $50) + 웹사이트·이메일 $2,000 + 광고 $5,000 = $10,000. 6주 시점 광고 예산 잔액 $1,500은 가정입니다.
도달·빈도 계산: 200,000명 × 1회 = 25,000명 × 8회 = 200,000회 노출. 두 선택지의 노출 수가 같도록 맞췄습니다(1,000회 노출당 $25 가정). 실제 광고 단가는 플랫폼·국가·시기에 따라 크게 다르므로 카드에 단가를 적지 않았습니다.
퍼널 수치: 방문 4,000 → 디자인 시작 900(22.5%) → 주문 30(디자인 시작자의 약 3.3%). 모두 가상 수치입니다. 결과 카드에는 개선 후 수치를 만들어 넣지 않고 정성적으로만 서술했습니다.

cards.title: You have $10,000 to launch. Where does it go?
body: You run a 30-person box factory. Most of your boxes go to a few big customers by the truckload.

Now you've built a simple website where small online shops can design printed shipping boxes and order as few as 100. You have **$10,000** and 90 days to launch it. Four decisions will decide where the money goes.

image.label: A small factory with a stack of printed boxes and a laptop
image.brief: 3D 클레이 스타일. 골판지 공장 바닥에 인쇄된 작은 배송 상자가 쌓여 있고, 그 위에 노트북 화면으로 상자 디자인 도구가 열려 있음. 옆에 "$10,000" 라벨이 붙은 돈 봉투. 실제 브랜드 로고는 쓰지 않음.

cards.title: Who should the launch speak to first?
body: Almost any business that ships things could use your boxes. But $10,000 can't speak to all of them.

options.text: Every small business that ships anything
options.feedback: You reach the most people, but your message has to be so general that it means little to anyone. The money spreads thin across people who don't care how a box looks.

options.text: Online gift and beauty sellers shipping 50–500 orders a month
options.feedback: These sellers care about the unboxing moment and order in small runs, exactly what your site does. You give up breadth to get a message that lands.

options.text: Large online brands with big shipping volumes
options.feedback: They buy a lot, but they want truckloads and long negotiations. That's your old business, not this launch.

cards.title: Say you chose gift and beauty sellers. Now split the money.
body: Same $10,000. Three ways to spend it.

image.label: Budget split into samples, website and ads
image.brief: 돈 더미 하나가 세 갈래로 나뉘는 인포그래픽. "Samples $3,000", "Website + email $2,000", "Ads $5,000". 샘플 상자를 열어 영상을 찍는 판매자 일러스트를 한쪽에 작게.

options.feedback: You buy attention fast, but it stops the day the money does. And strangers see an ad from a factory they've never heard of, with nobody vouching for it.

options.text: $3,000 on sample boxes for 60 sellers who post unboxing videos, $2,000 on the website and an email list, $5,000 on ads
options.feedback: Samples can turn into posts you didn't pay for. The site and email list stay yours after launch. Ads fill the gaps. Each part does a different job.

options.text: A $10,000 booth at a big packaging trade show
options.feedback: You'd meet serious buyers, but mostly large brands ordering by the truckload. The small sellers you chose rarely go.

cards.title: Say you chose the mix. Now aim the $5,000 in ads.
body: The ad tool offers about 200,000 ad views for your money. How do you spread them?

options.text: Reach 200,000 small business owners, once each
options.feedback: Wide and shallow. Most people need to see a new name several times before they act, and most of these owners don't sell gifts anyway.

options.text: Reach about 25,000 gift and beauty sellers, about eight times each over 90 days
options.feedback: Same 200,000 views, aimed at likely buyers and repeated enough to be remembered. You give up the feeling of being everywhere.

options.text: Spend it all in week one for a big splash
options.feedback: A splash can create buzz. But sellers who weren't ready to reorder boxes that week never see you again.

cards.title: Six weeks in, the numbers arrive.
body: 4,000 people visited the site. 900 started designing a box. Only **30** ordered. You still have $1,500 of ad money left. What do you do first?

image.label: A funnel: 4,000 visits, 900 designs, 30 orders
image.brief: 깔때기 그림. 위에서부터 "Visited 4,000", "Started a design 900", "Ordered 30". 맨 아래 칸에서 물방울이 새어 나가는 모습으로 이탈을 표현.

options.text: Spend the $1,500 on more ads to bring more visitors
options.feedback: More people pour into the same leak. If only 30 of 900 designers buy, more visitors mostly means more people leaving.

options.text: Watch where designers quit, and call ten of them
options.feedback: You find the problem before paying to repeat it. Here, most quit at checkout, where a $60 setup fee and shipping appeared for the first time.

options.text: Redesign the site to look more premium
options.feedback: It might help, but it's a guess. Nothing in the numbers says looks are the problem.

cards.title: Fixing the leak beat buying more traffic.
body: You showed the full price, setup fee and shipping included, on the first screen. Fewer people started a design. More of those who did finished the order.
The cheapest growth in a launch is often at the step where people already leave. You paid to bring them that far.
cards.softwareNote: Software launches show the same pattern between sign-up and first payment. A surprise at the paywall loses people you already paid to attract.

cards.title: Your real numbers won't look like these.
body: Ad prices vary a lot by platform, country and season, and an ad tool's reach figures are estimates. Samples only earn posts if the product is worth showing.
A narrow target also has a ceiling. Once you've reached most gift sellers, growth needs a new group.
And notice why decision 4 was possible: some money was still unspent. **Keep part of any launch budget back** for what you learn.

cards.title: A launch budget is four choices, made in order.
body: Each choice narrowed the next. Here's where each one came from in this unit:
cards.callout: **Try it today:** before your next campaign, write one line each: who it's for, which mix, how often they'll see it, and which step you'll watch.
